guide.title: Wilderness Club: Golf in Eureka, Montana
guide.intro: Golf Digest's 2025-'26 Best in State ranking lists Wilderness Club fifth in Montana, the highest-ranked course carrying Golf Digest's own "Public" label — the four courses ranked above it, Rock Creek Cattle Company, The Reserve At Moonlight Basin, Stock Farm Club and Iron Horse Golf Club, are all labelled "Private." Wilderness Club is in Eureka, Lincoln County, at 1885 Sophie Lake Rd, designed by Nick Faldo and opened in 2009. In the 2026 season the course's own FAQ states it is open to non-member and non-resort-guest play after 12:00 PM — no membership or resort room required — though the operator, Escalante Golf, LLC, has said publicly it intends to eventually return the club to fully private status. Eureka's other public course, Indian Springs Ranch Golf Course, lies two miles north on Highway 93 and gives this guide a second round.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body: U.S. Route 93 reaches its northern terminus at the Canada–US border near Eureka, and the highway runs south through Whitefish and Kalispell. Eureka to Whitefish is 51 miles, southeast, following the US-93 route. Eureka to Glacier Park International Airport (FCA), near Kalispell, is 63 miles via US-93. Wilderness Club itself, at 1885 Sophie Lake Rd, is eight miles from the Canadian border.

sections.heading: Wilderness Club
sections.body: Golf Digest's 2025-'26 Best in State ranking places Wilderness Club fifth in Montana — the highest-ranked course the magazine labels "Public"; the four courses ranked above it, Rock Creek Cattle Company, The Reserve At Moonlight Basin, Stock Farm Club and Iron Horse Golf Club, are all labelled "Private." Golf Digest also lists the course #57 in America's 100 Greatest Public Golf Courses (2025-'26). Nick Faldo designed the course, which opened in 2009. The operator publishes: "four tee box positions from 5431 to over 7200 yards allow play for all levels of experience"; other sources give the longest tee at 7,207 yards, par 72. The property spans roughly 550 acres. The operator's own golf page states: "For the comfort and safety of all of our golfers, dogs are not permitted on the golf course."

sections.heading: Playing it in 2026
sections.body: Wilderness Club's own FAQ, on thewildernessclub.com — the course's official site, its footer reading "© 2026 Escalante Golf, LLC" — answers plainly: "Can non-members play golf at the Wilderness Club? Yes, in the 2026 season. The golf course is open to non-member and non-resort-guest play after 12:00 PM." Tee times can be booked at wildernessclub.ezlinksgolf.com or by calling (406) 296-8264; neither a club membership nor a resort room is required. The course opens in early April and closes at the end of October, depending on weather. No dated green fee is published anywhere on the operator's site for Wilderness Club; the price is a genuine gap in the record and must be confirmed when booking. A separate sentence on the same operator's site, aimed at prospective buyers of homes in the surrounding development, states that golf amenities "will be privately owned and operated as a club with mandatory membership and mandatory membership fees payable." That sentence sits inside a real-estate offering disclaimer for the residential community and does not describe the golf-access policy above. In March 2024, Fort Worth Inc. reported: "Escalante's plans also involve transitioning Wilderness Club back to a fully private club, its founder's original vision. Currently, Wilderness Club is a semi-private club." That is a stated intention dated 2024, not the rule in effect for the 2026 season — a visitor planning ahead should know the afternoon-access policy above could change.

sections.heading: Day two: Indian Springs Ranch
sections.body: Indian Springs Ranch Golf Course, at 3082 Montana Highway 93 North, lies two miles north of Eureka on Highway 93. Visit Montana, the state tourism office, labels it a "PUBLIC GOLF COURSE." The Montana State Golf Association records that "Indian Springs was first opened to the public in 2010." It plays 18 holes at 6,600 yards. The operator's published 2026 season rates run April 1 through October 31, 2026: $90 for eighteen holes, or $110 with a cart, with range balls included. Tee times can be booked up to seven days ahead by calling (406) 889-5056.

faq.question: Can I play Wilderness Club without a membership?
faq.answer: Yes, in the 2026 season. The course's own FAQ states: "Can non-members play golf at the Wilderness Club? Yes, in the 2026 season. The golf course is open to non-member and non-resort-guest play after 12:00 PM." No club membership and no resort room booking is required.

faq.question: How do I book a tee time at Wilderness Club?
faq.answer: Book at wildernessclub.ezlinksgolf.com or by calling (406) 296-8264. Tee times for non-members and non-resort-guests start after 12:00 PM in the 2026 season.

faq.question: What does a round cost at Wilderness Club?
faq.answer: No dated green fee is published anywhere on the operator's site. This is a genuine gap in the record, not an omission of convenience — confirm the price when you book.

faq.question: When is Wilderness Club open?
faq.answer: The operator states: "We typically open The Wilderness Golf Course in early April and close at the end of October, depending on weather." A winter round is not possible.

faq.question: Is Wilderness Club going private?
faq.answer: The operator, Escalante Golf, has stated an intention to do so. In March 2024, Fort Worth Inc. reported that Escalante's plans "also involve transitioning Wilderness Club back to a fully private club, its founder's original vision." That is a 2024 statement of intent, not the rule in effect for the 2026 season, which is the afternoon-access policy above. A visitor planning ahead should confirm the policy still holds before travelling.

faq.question: What is the "mandatory membership" language I might see on the club's site?
faq.answer: It is a real-estate disclaimer aimed at buyers of homes in the surrounding development, stating that golf amenities "will be privately owned and operated as a club with mandatory membership and mandatory membership fees payable." It describes the residential community's real-estate offering, not the golf-access rule — the same site's FAQ separately confirms non-member, non-resort-guest play after 12:00 PM in the 2026 season.

faq.question: Where can I book a second round near Eureka?
faq.answer: Indian Springs Ranch Golf Course, two miles north of Eureka on Highway 93, is a straightforwardly public 18 holes. The operator's 2026 season rates are $90 for eighteen holes or $110 with a cart, April 1 through October 31, 2026; tee times can be booked up to seven days ahead by calling (406) 889-5056.
